syllabus: SYNTHETIC TEST MATERIAL. CHEM 241 Organic Chemistry I, Fall 2026. Instructor: Dr. Marguerite Okonkwo-Hale. Office: Brandt Hall 312. Office hours: Tue/Thu 2:00-3:30 PM or by appointment. Email: mokonkwohale@fictional-univ.edu. Meets MWF 10:00-10:50 AM, Science Center 140. Textbook: Organic Chemistry, 4th ed., Vance and Lindqvist (fictional). A molecular model kit is strongly recommended. COURSE DESCRIPTION: Structure, bonding, and reactivity of organic molecules. Topics include acid-base chemistry, nomenclature, conformations, stereochemistry, substitution and elimination reactions, and an introduction to alkene chemistry. WEEKLY SCHEDULE: Week 1 (Aug 24): Course intro, atomic structure, covalent bonding, Lewis structures. Week 2 (Aug 31): Formal charge, resonance, hybridization. Week 3 (Sep 7; no class Mon Sep 7, Labor Day): Acids and bases, pKa. Week 4 (Sep 14): Alkane nomenclature, functional groups. Week 5 (Sep 21): Intermolecular forces, acid-base wrap-up. Week 6 (Sep 28): Conformations of alkanes, Newman projections. Week 7 (Oct 5): Cycloalkanes, chair cyclohexane, ring flips. Week 8 (Oct 12): Chirality, enantiomers, R/S assignment. Week 9 (Oct 19): Diastereomers, meso compounds, optical activity. Week 10 (Oct 26): Alkyl halides, SN2 mechanism. Week 11 (Nov 2): SN1 mechanism, carbocation stability; midterm review. Week 12 (Nov 9): Substitution vs. elimination, E1. Week 13 (Nov 16): E2, Zaitsev rule. Week 14 (Nov 23; no class Thu-Fri Nov 26-27, Thanksgiving): Alkene structure and stability. Week 15 (Nov 30): Electrophilic addition to alkenes. Week 16 (Dec 7): Review and synthesis problems. QUIZZES (in class, 20 minutes, Fridays): Quiz 1, Fri Sep 11: Lewis structures, formal charge, resonance. Quiz 2, Fri Sep 25: Acid-base reactions, pKa, alkane nomenclature. Quiz 3, Fri Oct 23: Stereochemistry (chirality, R/S, enantiomers, diastereomers, meso). Quiz 4, Fri Nov 13: SN1 and SN2 reactions. Quiz 5, Fri Dec 4: Elimination reactions and alkene addition. The lowest quiz score is dropped. MIDTERM EXAM: Wed Nov 4, 7:00-8:30 PM, Science Center 140. Covers Weeks 1-10. FINAL EXAM: Tue Dec 15, 8:00-10:00 AM, Science Center 140. Cumulative, with emphasis on Weeks 10-16. GRADING: Homework (weekly online sets) 15%. Quizzes (best 4 of 5) 20%. Participation (clicker questions) 10%. Midterm exam 25%. Final exam 30%. Total 100%. Grade cutoffs: A 90+, B 80-89, C 70-79, D 60-69, F below 60. POLICIES: 1) Late homework loses 10% per day, up to 3 days, after which it is not accepted. The two lowest homework scores are dropped. 2) Makeup quizzes or exams are given only with documented illness or an excused university activity, and you must email the instructor before the exam time. 3) Academic integrity: all exams are closed-book and closed-notes. Only a molecular model kit and a non-programmable calculator are allowed. Any violation is reported to the Dean of Students. Dates may change with announcement in class and on the course page.
notes: CHEM 241 notes - Jasmine. TOPIC 1: Acids & bases. Bronsted acid = H+ donor, base = H+ acceptor. Lewis acid = e- pair acceptor, Lewis base = e- pair donor. Lower pKa = stronger acid. Rxn favors the side w/ the weaker acid (higher pKa) -> eq lies toward the more stable conj base. Ex: acetic acid pKa ~4.8, water ~15.7, so AcOH + HO- goes way forward. Factors for conj base stability (ARIO): Atom (EN and size; across a row EN wins, down a column size wins, so HI > HBr > HCl > HF acidity), Resonance, Inductive (EWG like F, Cl nearby help), Orbital (sp > sp2 > sp3, alkyne H pKa ~25). Rule: pKa diff of 10 -> 10^10 K, don't need the calc just compare. Dr. O-H said memorize pKa ranges: carboxylic acid ~5, phenol ~10, alcohol ~16, ketone alpha-H ~20, alkyne ~25, amine N-H ~35, alkane ~50. Marked: THIS IS ON QUIZ 2 (already done, got 17/20, oops forgot the resonance on phenoxide). TOPIC 2: Cyclohexane conformations. Chair = most stable, ~0 angle strain, all staggered. Boat & twist-boat higher E (flagpole H's clash). Each C has axial (up/down alternating) and equatorial H. Ring flip swaps ax <-> eq, cis/trans stays the same. Big groups want equatorial to avoid 1,3-diaxial interactions (steric). A-values: methyl 1.7 kcal/mol, t-butyl ~5 (basically locked eq), Br ~0.4. Methylcyclohexane: ~95% eq at RT. Disubstituted: draw both chairs, count ax groups, lower # of big ax groups wins. Ex: cis-1,4 -> one ax one eq (a,e) both chairs. Trans-1,4 -> diequatorial (e,e) or diaxial (a,a), e,e favored. Tip: draw chair w/ the right-pointing 'up' carbon first, practice w/ model kit. TO DO: redo HW 8 problems 4-7 on Newman projections, go to office hrs Thurs about chair drawing.
photoText: Whiteboard photo - SN2 mechanism. SN2 = bimolecular, one step, concerted. Rate = k [RX] [Nuc]. Nucleophile attacks from the backside (180 deg from leaving group) -> inversion of conf1guration (Walden inversion). Transition state: pentacoordinate carbon, partial bonds to Nuc and LG, sp2-like. Steric hlndrance matters: methyl > 1° > 2° >> 3° (3° does not react). Good LG = weak bases (I-, Br-, TsO-). Good Nuc in polar aprotic solvents (DMSO, acetone, [unreadable]). Ex: (R)-2-bromobutane + CN- -> (S)-2-cyanobutane (inversion!). Draw eneray diagram: one hump, no intermediate. Solvent: polar aprotlc speeds SN2, polar protic cages the nuc via H-bonding and slows it. Compare w/ SN1: two steps, carbocatlon, racemlzation. Note: nucleophilicity ≠ basicity, but they trend together across a rcw.
